Lena to update admin runbook and share link to Confluence

transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-20 15:00 PDT — Duration: 45m
Attendees: Lena Park, Marcus Reed, Aisha Khan, Tom Ellis, Priya Patel, Samir Rao

[00:00] Lena: Alright everyone, thanks for hopping on. This is the weekly IT / Finance / Security admin sync. Quick run through agenda: Okta renewal budget, SOC 2 artifacts status, IAM maintenance window, and vendor invoice timing.
[00:18] Marcus: Hey, morning. I'll start with SOC 2. We got the draft from the auditor but there are a couple of control gaps still open, mostly around logging retention and new SSO onboarding process. Notes are in the tracker I shared.
[00:30] Aisha: I saw that — thanks. On the finance side, we got the preliminary numbers. The Okta renewal is up next quarter; procurement needs a yes/no from finance by end of month or we'll need to push the payment schedule.
[00:45] Tom: Quick clarifying Q — when you say logging retention, is that storage cost or policy change?
[00:52] Marcus: Mostly policy and retention configuration in centralized logging. There's also a small estimated cost increase if we keep logs for three years vs one year, because of S3 retention — costs are not huge but we need to surface them to finance.
[01:08] Aisha: ballpark?
[01:10] Marcus: Off the top, maybe 8 to 12k a year for long term retention depending on compression and access patterns. I'll put a better estimate in the tracker.
[01:20] Priya: For procurement, we also need updated vendor terms for Okta: can we get an updated SSO user count and any new modules? That affects the tiering.
[01:30] Lena: We plan to onboard about 60 more service accounts for automated deployments and a couple of extra admin seats for the security team. So yes, tier might shift.
[01:40] Samir: Also want to flag key management — we need to confirm if the Okta integration touches any encrypted credentials stored in our KMS/HSM. If so, update the key rotation docs.
[01:52] Marcus: Good point. The app integrations do use a couple of service keys; I can map them.
[02:00] --- brief pause / background noise ---
[02:12] Tom: Switching to IAM maintenance window — suggested week of April 6th, low traffic. We'd need 2 hours of degraded SSO during nightly window. Thoughts?
[02:23] Aisha: Two hours sounds fine if it's at 3am PT, but need confirmation on runbook and incident contact.
[02:30] Lena: I'll create the runbook update and include rollback steps. We should also notify the CS and platform teams.
[02:40] Marcus: One risk — if the migration step touches the KV cache for sessions, tokens may be invalidated and apps without graceful reauth could fail. We should list high-risk services.
[02:52] Tom: We'll run a smoke test and have a quick rollback plan.
[03:00] Lena: ok, action: Tom to book the window and run the smoke test, Marcus to list high-risk services.
[03:08] Marcus: moving on to invoices: we have a couple of vendor invoices that hit the ticketing that aren't coded to the right cost center. Aisha?
[03:16] Aisha: Yes, the cloud infra charge accidentally went to the product team cost center. Finance will reclassify but we need procurement to confirm the PO numbers.
[03:25] Priya: I can cross-check POs and resend to finance.
[03:30] Lena: Any security reviews pending? Samir?
[03:34] Samir: We have one incoming request from a customer success tool that wants access to logs for debug. Need to confirm SSO/SCIM provisioning, and what log levels are exposed. Also check data residency — some customer data must remain in EU.
[03:48] Marcus: We need to ensure log redaction is applied for PII before sharing. There's also the question about audit logs retention policy for shared support access — currently 90 days.
[04:00] Aisha: If customers require longer retention for audit, that increases cost; procurement needs to know.
[04:08] Tom: Are we on track for the security questionnaire due next month? I thought some items were outstanding.
[04:14] Samir: Right, the vendor security questionnaire — we have open items on encryption-at-rest details, key management, and RBAC segmentation. Marcus has been filling in, but I need final signoff.
[04:24] Marcus: I'm compiling the encryption details (KMS, AES-256, HSM for private keying) — will add diagrams.
[04:30] Lena: Good. On the Okta renewal again, Aisha, what's the runway for approval?
[04:36] Aisha: We can push approvals internally but need a formal PO by 2026-03-31 to make the vendor deadline. If finance doesn't get budget confirmation by 2026-03-26 I can't commit.
[04:48] Priya: We'll try to get the draft contract in 10 days.
[04:52] Lena: Need to sync on SSO provisioning timeline — is that tied to the renewal?
[04:56] Marcus: Partly. If we change tiers or add modular features, provisioning calls might change. Also need to test SCIM for group sync.
[05:06] --- transcript notes: speakers overlap, occasional crosstalk ---
[05:18] Tom: Quick Q on backups — we had that one incident; are backups encrypted and are recovery tests scheduled?
[05:24] Marcus: Backups are encrypted at rest with customer-managed keys in KMS; recovery tests were last done in January, we plan monthly drills. I'll confirm next test date.
[05:34] Aisha: If recovery drill shows gaps, that could impact compliance.
[05:38] Marcus: noted.
[06:00] Lena: Any blockers from finance for the logging retention change?
[06:06] Aisha: Need clear estimate and justification for business need. If security says it's required for compliance we can probably find budget.
[06:14] Samir: It's partially compliance, partially for long-term forensic capability. We can provide examples of cases where longer retention helped.
[06:24] Priya: Also vendor negotiation point — we might push some storage to cold tier to save cost.
[06:30] Marcus: I'll include cold-tier estimate and access latency tradeoffs.
[06:36] --- timestamp jump ---
[10:00] Tom: On procurement timeline — I need a finalized PO line with user counts and modules for Okta by Friday.
[10:08] Aisha: Friday EOD is tight but achievable if Marcus and Lena finalize numbers by Thursday.
[10:16] Lena: I'll update runbook and the user count list tonight.
[10:22] Priya: I'll draft contract notes and send to Aisha for redlines.
[12:00] Marcus: Security note: audit logs need to be immutable for 90 days for internal policy; if customers request longer we mark it as exception handling with procurement.
[12:12] Samir: Also need to confirm SAML signing cert rotation frequency; we currently do annual rotation but some customers want six-month rotation.
[12:20] Marcus: It requires orchestration with the deployment pipelines; short rotation increases operational load.
[12:28] Aisha: Ok will note as potential extra operational cost.
[15:00] --- final recap ---
[15:05] Lena: Recap: Marcus to circulate SOC2 summary + gap tracker by 2026-03-24; Aisha to confirm budget by 2026-03-26; Tom to book maintenance window and run smoke test by 2026-03-30; Priya to draft vendor contract updates by 2026-04-02. We'll reconvene next week same time if there are blockers.
[15:30] Marcus: One more thing — I'll upload the updated encryption diagram to Confluence and tag Samir.
[15:40] Lena: Great, thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.
